title: Authorization decomposition and compact audit schema
content:
Summary:

This note sketches an approach to break RBAC v2 authorization down into compact primitives and defines a minimal, telemetry-friendly audit record that satisfies evidence automation and SIEM export requirements for high-throughput paths. Goal is to reduce cardinality and payload size in exported logs while preserving queryability for compliance and incident response.

Goals and constraints:
- Goals:
  - Provide a composable permission model (decomposition) that reduces duplication across services and enables fine-grained, testable mappings.
  - Design a compact audit/event schema that can be ingested by SIEM with minimal expansion (avoid megabyte JSON blobs per request).
  - Ensure evidence automation can reconstruct the decision chain for a given action: who requested, which attributes were used, which policy matched, and what derived attributes/fallbacks applied.
- Constraints:
  - Must be low-latency and small payloads for high-volume inference calls (token-level tracing is optional; keep per-request event small).
  - Backward compatibility with existing permission tags and some entitlement names for first-phase rollout.
  - Support private deployments that require on-prem export and configurable retention.

Principles for decomposition:
- Decompose authorization checks into three orthogonal axes: Resource, Operation, and Condition-set.
  - Resource: canonical resource type + stable id namespace (e.g., model:open-llm-3b or repo:customer-data).
  - Operation: atomized action verbs (e.g., generate, embed, view-metrics, upload-model). Avoid compound verbs.
  - Condition-set: a named predicate (attribute expression) that captures environment/context (e.g., internal-network, vpc-boundary, data-class-pii).
- Attach short, stable IDs to named condition-sets and policies to keep audit records compact (see compact IDs below).

Permission identity and mapping:
- Permission = <resource-type>::<operation>::<condition-id>
  - Example: model::generate::cond-03 (where cond-03 expands to "customer-vpc AND not-preview-mode")
- Maintain a central registry that maps permission names to policy ids and human-friendly descriptions. The registry will be small and can be referenced by id in logs.

Policy evaluation contract (observable):
- Each eval returns a compact decision tuple: <decision>, <policy_id>, <matched_attributes_id>, <evidence_id?>
  - decision: allow|deny|defer
  - policy_id: short id (p-024)
  - matched_attributes_id: short id referencing the attribute bundle used during the decision (a digest)
  - evidence_id: optional pointer to a larger artifact stored in evidence-bucket (only when requested or on violation)
- The enforcement library must synchronously emit a one-line audit record (see schema) and optionally push a richer artifact into the evidence store asynchronously.

Compact audit schema (single-line JSON, optimized for SIEM ingestion):
- Fields (all short names to save bytes):
  - ts: ISO8601 timestamp (string)
  - uid: user id (string) or svc id for machine calls
  - tid: trace id / request id (string)
  - res: resource string (short form, e.g., model:open-llm-3b)
  - op: operation (generate/embed/modify)
  - dec: decision (A=allow, D=deny, X=deferred)
  - pid: policy_id (p-024)
  - mid: matched_attributes_id (a short hex digest)
  - ev: evidence_ref (optional short url or s3 path)
  - src: request source (svc, console, api-key, ip-<masked>)
  - rv: rule_version (semver-like short, e.g., r1.4)
  - dur: decision latency in ms (integer)
  - tags: comma-delimited short tags (optional)
- Example single-line record:
  {"ts":"2024-12-01T15:23:12Z","uid":"u-1823","tid":"r-8f23a","res":"model:open-llm-3b","op":"generate","dec":"A","pid":"p-024","mid":"m-9f","ev":"s3://evidence/prd/p-024/r-8f23a.json","src":"api-key","rv":"r1.4","dur":12}

Design rationale:
- Short field names reduce storage and index pressure in SIEM.
- Linking to an evidence artifact only on exceptions or on-demand preserves performance and avoids creating large volumes of artifacts.
- Use small stable ids (p-###, m-##) for cross-referencing; the registry allows analysts to expand ids when needed.

Evidence artifact format (when created):
- Stored as gzipped JSON in an evidence bucket or internal store. Minimal schema:
  - header: { policy_id, matched_attributes_id, ts, uid, tid, res, op }
  - attributes: full attribute map used in decision (principals, env, client ip, VPC id, token scope, etc.)
  - policy_snippet: the exact policy code or rule fingerprint that matched
  - evaluation_trace: optional step-by-step trace for debugging (time-ordered list)
  - raw_request: truncated request payload (only when necessary and scrubbed)
- Evidence artifacts are referenced by evidence_ref in the compact record. Evidence retention policy configurable by install: default 90 days for hosted; customers may opt-in for longer in Private.

SIEM export mapping and parsing guidance:
- Export the compact records directly as newline-delimited JSON. Provide a mapping script that expands p-### and m-## via a local registry snapshot injected into the SIEM parser pipeline.
- Important SIEM fields to materialize for analysts: ts, uid, res, op, dec, pid, ev, src. Keep other fields as metadata or searchable tags.
- Sampling policy: accept 1:1000 sampling for allowed decisions in heavy paths (generate), but ensure 100% export for denied/exceptional dec=D or X. Sampling rules are controlled by the export agent and documented in the registry.

Evidence automation rules and playbook:
- When to create evidence artifact (async):
  - dec == D (deny) OR dec == X OR (dec == A AND policy has high-sensitivity tag)
  - explicit audit request via governance API (ad-hoc capture)
- Automation steps for deny event:
  1) enforcement library emits compact record with evidence_ref placeholder.
  2) async agent collects full attribute bundle, policy snippet, and request context; stores gzipped artifact and writes back evidence_ref into a follow-up SIEM event or the evidence index.
  3) Alerting rules in SIEM pick up denies on sensitive resources and create incidents in PagerDuty/opsgenie.

Migration and rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: registry & library bootstrapping (2 weeks)
  - Create policy and condition-set registry with stable ids (p-*, m-*).
  - Implement enforcement library patch for compact audit emission (feature flagged).
- Phase 1: Canary + pilot teams (3–4 weeks)
  - Enable compact schema for internal platform-team models and one customer-facing model pool.
  - Run SIEM ingestion in parallel with legacy logs for parity checks.
- Phase 2: Controlled migration (4–8 weeks)
  - Expand to all model generation paths. Enable evidence artifacts for denies and sensitive policies.
  - Launch sampling agent for permitted events (1:1000 default) and monitor fidelity metrics.
- Phase 3: Deprecation of old audit blobs (2–4 weeks)
  - After parity demonstrated and queries validated, retire old verbose audit export. Keep a snapshot backup for 60 days.

Validation queries / success metrics:
- Parity: run weekly diff between legacy and compact exports to measure information loss (target <0.1% truncation of required fields).
- SIEM ingestion rate: compact schema should reduce byte-rate by >70% on high-volume routes.
- Evidence retrieval: ability to reconstruct decision end-to-end given one compact record + evidence artifact (when present).
- False negatives: ensure denied events always exported (target 100%).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Id namespace management: who owns p-* and m-* allocations? Proposal: central security registry team issues ids and PR flow via GitHub.
- Sampling policy configuration granularity: global vs per-policy. Recommend per-policy sampling config in registry.
- Retention defaults for Private installs where customers may require different retention; add UI hooks in Console.

Action items (next steps):
- Samir: draft registry schema (due 2024-11-22)
- Lena: prototype enforcement library emitting compact record (POC by 2024-12-01)
- Ethan: prototype SIEM parser with registry expansion (PR by 2024-12-12)
- Priya: define evidence storage lifecycle and KMS integration notes (due 2024-12-05)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc; I'm intentionally favoring compactness in the exported record to reduce SIEM costs. Expect follow-ups on naming conventions (p- vs pol-) and attribute digest generation.
- Please reply with objections on sampling defaults and id allocation model.

End of doc.
